title: Relationship Directionality
description: Demonstrates unidirectional and bidirectional relationships (§8.11). Three domains: (1) unidirectional Invoice→Customer — only the Invoice side holds a reference; (2) bidirectional Person↔Car — both sides reference each other, Car.ownerId is the authoritative owning side; (3) mixed vertical+horizontal bidirectional — Report embeds Sections vertically while each Section carries a horizontal back-reference ID to its containing Report.

Customer.title: Customer
Customer.description: Domain 1 — Unidirectional. TARGET side: Customer has no knowledge of which Invoices reference it. It can be updated without touching any Invoice.

Invoice.title: Invoice
Invoice.description: Domain 1 — Unidirectional. SOURCE side: holds a reference to its Customer via customerId. Navigation is possible only in one direction: Invoice → Customer. To find all Invoices for a Customer the application must query by customerId.

customerId.description: UNIDIRECTIONAL HAS-ONE HORIZONTAL → Customer. No back-reference exists on Customer.

Person.title: Person
Person.description: Domain 2 — Bidirectional horizontal. INVERSE side of the Person↔Car relationship. Person.carIds is a convenience back-reference maintained by the application. Car.ownerId is the owning (authoritative) side; when the two ends disagree Car.ownerId takes precedence by convention.

carIds.description: BIDIRECTIONAL HAS-MANY HORIZONTAL ↔ Car (inverse side). The application must keep this in sync with Car.ownerId. OOJS does not enforce consistency between the two ends.

Car.title: Car
Car.description: Domain 2 — Bidirectional horizontal. OWNING side of the Person↔Car relationship. Car.ownerId is the authoritative source of truth for the ownership link.

ownerId.description: BIDIRECTIONAL HAS-ONE HORIZONTAL ↔ Person (owning side). Navigate: Car → Person. Authoritative source of truth for the ownership relationship.

Section.title: Section
Section.description: Domain 3 — Mixed vertical+horizontal bidirectional. Embedded inside Report (vertical has-many). Also carries a horizontal back-reference (reportId) so that a Section retrieved in isolation can navigate back to its containing Report. OOJS does not verify that section.reportId matches the ID of its enclosing Report.

reportId.description: BACK-REFERENCE (horizontal): the ID of the Report this Section belongs to. Enables Section → Report navigation. Must be kept consistent with the enclosing Report's reportId by the application.

Report.title: Report
Report.description: Domain 3 — Mixed vertical+horizontal bidirectional. Embeds its Sections vertically (owning side). Each Section also carries a back-reference reportId to enable navigation from Section → Report without parsing the full Report document.

sections.description: HAS-MANY VERTICAL (owning side). Sections are embedded and fully validated here. The inverse navigation (Section → Report) is via Section.reportId.
